name: Budj Bim Cultural Landscape
description: In south-western Victoria, Australia, Budj Bim is a dormant volcano whose ancient lava flows were shaped by the Gunditjmara people into a vast network of channels, weirs and dams. They used it to trap and farm kooyang, the short-finned eel, feeding their communities for around six thousand years. It is among the world's oldest and most extensive aquaculture systems, and Gunditjmara knowledge of it is still passed on today.
